entities.name: PMID:25081811
observations: Error-corrected NGS of HCV E1/E2 from 58 chronically infected patients yielded a mean of 3,202 reads and 464 variants per sample.
Variant networks connected sequences differing by one nucleotide; components containing >5% of reads captured 93.7% of reads on average.
Large connected components occurred within hosts, but multiple distinct separated components were present rather than one network spanning all variants.

entities.name: Large HCV components
observations: NGS can reveal large connected components of intra-host HCV variants, but the reported architecture is fragmented into multiple separated components rather than a single all-variant network.

entities.name: PMID:29244001
observations: HVR1 ultra-deep sequencing and k-step networks showed that Hamming centrality correlated with transmissibility, but the available evidence did not establish a single large or star-like within-host topology.
